sourceObjective: Indirect objects: to whom?: Me, te, le, nos and les can identify the recipient: le doy el libro a Ana.
sourceSpeaking: Role-play Compartir materiales with a patient classmate. Practice indirect objects: to whom?. Use this lesson's grammar, ask a related question, answer the partner, and confirm understanding. Keep language at beginner level; explain unfamiliar words in English when asked.

cards.candidateNote: French me may be an object or reflexive clitic depending on construction; emphatic myself is moi-même.
French te may be an object or reflexive clitic depending on construction; emphatic yourself is toi-même.
La can be feminine article or object pronoun depending on the sentence.
Spanish los is masculine plural. French les is both masculine and feminine, article or direct-object pronoun, not the indirect recipient clitic leur.
Élèves / étudiants are contextual alternatives, not one positionally scored face.

sourceVersusFrenchNote: The pinned objective describes Spanish indirect objects. Spanish indirect le/les typically correspond to French lui/leur; French les in card 6 is an article or direct-object pronoun and covers any plural gender. Full noun recipients use à/aux in this Reader; clitic recipients me/t’/nous do not. The Spanish objective is not itself a French grammar rule.
